text:
In his second season in Carolina, Nikolaj Ehlers has turned into a setup man. He has 20 points in 21 games but only 5 goals, and three more assists in Saturday's win over Seattle in Helsinki pushed his last ten games to 12 points (2 goals, 10 assists) against an expected 8.1.

That run is a little generous. Carolina has scored 3.3 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. His own finishing, 5 goals on 5.8 expected, is right where it should be. Half his points have come on the power play.

His five-on-five numbers relative to teammates are slightly negative, which says more about how deep this Carolina lineup is than about him: Evolving-Hockey ranked him 16th among forwards in wins above replacement last season and credited him with taking chances away, 90th percentile.

The tell is in the passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 97th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists, and 52% of his own shots came off the rush. Watch him in the first few seconds after Carolina wins the puck back. Our projection has him finishing with about 72 points.
